incident-bot: INCIDENT: serving-runtime - multi-GPU jobs failing: NCCL communicator errors and CUDA OOMs detected. Paging on-call. Severity: P1. Affected: inference-pool-tp, several dedicated pods.

alex (oncall): I’m on it. seeing repeated `ncclComm` timeouts and a few container OOM kills from the same node pool.

priya (runtime): add context: this looks like tensor-parallel jobs hitting collective hangs during step sync. stack shows NCCL timeout then CUDA driver internal error.

sam (infra): node metrics show intermittent PCIe errors on node-gpu-12 and high GPU memory fragmentation. logs: ```
[2026-03-15T02:13:45Z] nccl: unhandled error, ncclCommAbort
[2026-03-15T02:13:45Z] cuda: cuCtxSynchronize() failed: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
[2026-03-15T02:13:46Z] container runtime: killed process 1 (python) SIGKILL (OOM)
```

jing (mlops): impact note: three customer inference endpoints (cust-a, cust-b, cust-c) routed to this TP pool are seeing elevated latency and 502s when the job hangs. traffic rerouted to CPU fallback for cust-c only so far.

priya (runtime): immediate mitigation plan: 1) disable NCCL P2P to force host staging (may increase latency but avoids nvlink/peer hangs) 2) toggle NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 to get cleaner aborts 3) restart affected TP pods gracefully and drain node-gpu-12 4) if IB/rdma is implicated, fall back by setting NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1.

alex (oncall): execute 1 & 2 now. I'll take node drain.

sam (infra): performing drain: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-12 && kubectl drain node-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` 

priya (runtime): patch we're applying to the serving runtime config (deploy rollout): ```yaml
env:
  - name: NCCL_P2P_DISABLE
    value: "1"
  - name: NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING
    value: "1"
  - name: NCCL_DEBUG
    value: "INFO"
```
Applying canary to pool=tp subset.

jing (mlops): quick note: also observed `NCCL WARN Call to -pthread` in older kernel; make sure nodes are on 5.15+ kernel.

marco (customer-ops): just told cust-a we’re investigating and routing to a replica pool; they reported 40% request failures for 20 minutes. cust-b seeing intermittent errors.

sam (infra): after drain, gimmed a node flap event on node-gpu-14; cluster autoscaler restarted a node. I'm watching.

priya (runtime): after canary patch rollouts 3/5 canaries completed successfully, 2 failed with same nccl timeout. rolling back the 2 and expanding canary to other nodes without nvlink (set label `nvlink=false`).

alex (oncall): handing off to priya for extended mitigation and postmortem. I'll stay reachable for escalation. Assigning pager to priya for the next 6h. @priyaa (typo intentionally avoided: use display name priya (runtime)). :pager:

priya (runtime): thanks. current mitigations in flight: - canary env patch - node drains for nodes with PCIe errors - route high-priority customer traffic to dedicated single-GPU variant for affected customers - enable extended NCCL logging for 1h: `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`

jing (mlops): collecting core dumps and nv_peer_mem logs; storing to /mnt/diag/1768800123/ for postmortem.

marco (customer-ops): customers updated: cust-a moved to warm replica pool, cust-b on degraded service, cust-c on CPU fallback. ETA for full recovery unknown.

priya (runtime): temporary mitigation results: after disabling P2P and restarting, two TP jobs recovered and resumed. we still have 1 reproducible job that hits `ncclCommDestroy` stuck state — investigating memory leak in kernel launch patterns.

sam (infra): note: applied `export NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` on one canary host — that instance stopped hitting nccl timeouts but CPU/GPU bandwidth changed; watch perf.

alex (oncall): customers still affected but severity lowered to P2 due to routing/fallbacks. keep paging only for regression.

priya (runtime): next actions for follow-up: 1) gather full kernel stacks and CUDA mem usage for the affected PID 2) reproduce in isolated staging with same batch shapes and TP config 3) run with NCCL_DEBUG=TRACE if we need deeper traces 4) recommend patch: enforce GPU memory defrag between steps and increase NCCL timeout threshold while we root cause.

marco (customer-ops): logging: cust-a asked for incident timeline; will need root cause and mitigation note for postmortem.

jing (mlops): creating incident ticket INC-1768800123 in tracker and attaching diag tarball.

priya (runtime): marking current thread: mitigated but not fully resolved. leaving runtime hooks and logs for postmortem.

alex (oncall): closing pager for immediate escalation. Priya owns follow-up and postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, customer impact reduced. Postmortem scheduled.

priya (runtime): postmortem action items I'm assigning: - increase NCCL timeout default for TP jobs - add automated detection for repeated ncclComm timeouts and auto-fallback to single-GPU variant - investigate kernel driver anomalies on nodes that showed PCIe errors - decide whether nvlink/fabric should be disabled by default on certain instance types.

marco (customer-ops): will draft customer-facing summary and share with legal/compliance if needed.

jing (mlops): end of thread notes: saved logs, assigned SEVs and owners, ticket created.

alex (oncall): thanks team. dropping off.
